Method of Attack: Poisoning Google search autocomplete suggestions to drive traffic to misleading sites, malware, or other malicious content
Two-stage attack: poisoning autocomplete suggestions and poisoning search results listings
Automated search queries in headless browsers across different IP addresses or human operators to manipulate suggestions
Discoverer: A team of academics from three US universities
Indicators of Compromise: Over 383K manipulated suggestions across 257K triggers found
At least 0.48% of Google autocomplete results polluted
Over 3,000 malicious sites in search results listings linked to poisoned suggestions
